🚨🇲🇽 <u>ALBERTO "VIRUS" RODRÍGUEZ — NUEVO IMPERIO BOSS BEHIND AZCAPOTZALCO VIOLENCE — DETAINED IN HIDALGO</u>

A coordinated federal-CDMX operation tracked Alberto Rodríguez, alias "Virus," from Azcapotzalco to Tulancingo, Hidalgo, where authorities arrested him without firing a shot. Investigators identify him as a leader of the Nuevo Imperio cell that triggered the recent spike in violence in the Mexico City borough. Brugada's CDMX administration reports high-impact crime down 65 percent vs. 2019 across the city — including a 51 percent drop in homicides and 16 alcaldías now showing reductions. This is what the Conferencia Nacional para la Construcción de Paz looks like in practice: arrests over executions, intelligence over Calderón-era theatrics.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>OFAC + UIF NOW WATCH 39 CASINO GROUPS IN MEXICO — CALIENTE, TV AZTECA, CODERE, IMAGEN ALL ON THE LIST</u>

The U.S. Treasury's OFAC and Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit are jointly monitoring the 39 business groups that control Mexico's authorized casinos and betting houses — including Jorge Hank Rhon's Grupo Caliente, TV Azteca's apuestas arm, Codere México, and the Vázquez Aldir / Grupo Imagen-linked Apuestas Internacionales — to lock down cartel money laundering. The Cártel del Noreste has been linked to Centenario and Diamante casinos; the Sinaloa cartel to Emine, Mirage, Midas, Palermo, and Skampa. Mexico's SAT pulled 74 billion pesos in IVA/ISR from the 39 groups in 2025, and the UIF slapped them with 6 billion in fines. Fiscal Procurator Grisel Galeano García detailed a six-step laundering scheme — stolen identities, prepaid cards, fake gaming winnings, transfers to tax havens. The Salinas-era casino-mafia complex that PAN governments protected is finally getting flayed open.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>TOPOLOBAMPO FISHERMEN SAY CONAPESCA CHIEF WALKED OUT — AMMONIA-PLANT FIGHT IN BAHÍA DE OHUIRA</u>

Sinaloa fishermen denounced today that the head of Conapesca, Rigoberto Salgado, skipped a scheduled technical roundtable with sea workers worried about the GPO ammonia plant being built in Bahía de Ohuira. "He distanced himself and avoided responding," fishermen said, after expecting answers about the plant's heated-water discharges that they warn will kill shrimp and crustaceans across the coastal lagoon. They also denounced the creation of "fraudulent" fishing cooperatives staged to legitimize the corporate project. The fight pits Topolobampo's coastal labor against a Swiss-Mexican petrochemical consortium — and exposes which side parts of the federal cabinet are leaning toward.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>SEP DEBUNKS OPPOSITION SMEAR: NO 800-MILLION-PESO "BRIBE" TO CNTE TO LIFT ZÓCALO PLANTÓN</u>

Mario Delgado shot down the right-wing media line that the federal government paid Section 22 of the CNTE 800 million pesos to evacuate the Zócalo. "There is no resource for the union. Everything goes through SEP's budget — not through the hands of the CNTE or the SNTE," the education secretary said today. The funds are budget items already approved for new teaching positions, hours, and recategorizations in Oaxaca, Chiapas, and Guerrero — the states with the country's largest education backlogs. The PRIAN tried to recycle Calderón-era "el sindicato cobró" playbooks — the federal budget says otherwise.
